newsitem.title: UK: EMU must be beneficial if UK to join - Major.
newsitem.headline: EMU must be beneficial if UK to join - Major.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major said on Wednesday supporters of a single European currency would have to show it was "positively beneficial" before Britain should consider signing up, the Press Association news agency reported.
It was not immediately clear in what context Major made the remark.
Earlier Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said Britain was on balance hostile to the idea of the new money.
Major, who was attending a launch in London for the European Year Against Racism, said it was incumbent upon those in favour of EMU to make their case.

"We would need to be persuaded that it was better. We are not so persuaded at the moment and we think it is very unlikely that the circumstances will be right by January 1, 1999, not just for us but right the way across Europe."
Earlier on Wednesday, Rifkind told BBC radio: "On balance we are hostile to a single currency, but we accept you have to think very carefully about these matters before you rule them out completely."
Major said he had not heard comments from Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke that Rifkind's comments were a "slip of the tongue".

But he stressed that the government's "wait and see" policy remained in place. "The Cabinet have an agreed position on the single currency which was agreed some time ago, the Chancellor agrees with it, the Foreign Secretary agrees, we all do."
